newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hogs in early direct trade sold steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with gains powered by light hog supplies and strong packer demand, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Packer demand was stoked by higher pork prices, particularly loins, which fueled talk of possible export business, they said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady-$0.50 higher at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $60.50 to $61.50 at plants. Illinois hogs sold $1.00 higher at $59.50-$60.00 in the country and $60.50-$61.00, possibly $62.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $60.50 to $61.00 at plants. Relatively light hog marketings were reported amid aggressive packer interest.
Ohio hogs sold up $0.50 at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants.

Pork cutout values on Tuesday were quoted up $0.55 to $0.62 per cwt, USDA said. Fresh loins weighing 14-22 lbs, with a 1/4-inch trim were up $3.00 at $156.50, compared with Monday, and up $5.50 from Friday, USDA statistics showed.
